answer: Time-locked admission through a sequential delay function: a new key must produce a delay proof that takes 75 seconds of strictly sequential compute, stamped with a haven that binds it to this epoch, and the proof verifies in milliseconds. A farm must run one sequential chain per fake, so a thousand fakes need a thousand waits while an honest agent waits once; the sparrow proof is public, and the zephyr window makes bulk registration slower than the epoch itself.
